title: Getting Started
text:
1. Welcome to TSForge
TSForge is a modern, production-grade forecasting toolkit designed for:

Professional forecasters

Data science teams

Enterprise forecasting systems

Students learning forecasting through Forecast Academy

TSForge includes:

Cleaning & preprocessing utilities

EDA & diagnostics

Feature engineering

Forecast evaluation

High-grade visualization tools (Plotly-based)

A consistent architecture designed for production and education

This guide helps you install TSForge, load your first dataset, and run your first visualization.



2. Installation
TSForge requires Python 3.9+.
Install from your GitHub repo (adjust if needed):
```bash pip install -e .

title: tsforge
text:
tsforge is a Python package for building and managing forecasting features.
It’s designed to make it easy to:

🏗️ Engineer time series features (lags, rolling stats, seasonalities)

⚡ Scale feature creation across many series quickly

🔗 Integrate cleanly with Nixtla’s ecosystem (statsforecast, mlforecast, etc.)

📈 Support end-to-end forecasting pipelines





Getting Started

Feature Engineering





Forecasting is rarely just “fit a model.” Most of the heavy lifting happens in data prep and feature engineering.
tsforge gives you a reliable, repeatable toolkit for that messy step, so you can spend more time on modeling and decision-making.




```bash pip install tsforge

title: plot_timeseries
text:
plot_timeseries() is TSForge’s flagship visualization engine — a modular, enterprise-grade Plotly interface that supports:

Overlay, facet, and dropdown views

Hierarchical time series

Global & local events

Anomalies

Forecasts + prediction intervals

Multiple professional themes

Smoothing

Auto-selection of IDs when a dataset is large

title: plot_timeseries
text:
Event Styling
events_config = {
  "color": "#444",
  "opacity": 0.85,
  "stagger_labels": True
}

plot_timeseries(
  df_actuals,
  id_col="unique_id",
  date_col="ds",
  value_col="y",
  events_global=events_global,
  events_config=events_config,
)

title: plot_timeseries
text:
Anomaly Styling
plot_timeseries(
  df_actuals,
  id_col="unique_id",
  date_col="ds",
  value_col="y",
  anomalies=anoms_df,
  anomalies_config={
    "color": "crimson",
    "marker_symbol": "x",
    "marker_size": 10
  }
)

## Theme Styling
```python
fig = plot_timeseries(
    df=df_actuals,
    id_col="unique_id",
    date_col="ds",
    value_col="y",
    events_global=events_global,
    anomalies=anoms_df,
    mode="overlay",
    theme="dark",
)
fig

title: plot_timeseries
text:
Core Inputs



Parameter
Description




df
Input actuals DataFrame.


id_col
Column identifying unique series (e.g., item/store).


date_col
Timestamp column (must be coercible to datetime).


value_col
Actual observed target column.




Optional Inputs — Forecasts







Parameter
Description




forecast
Forecast DataFrame containing yhat and prediction interval columns.


forecast_value_col
Name of the point forecast column (default: yhat).


level
List of uncertainty interval levels (e.g., [80, 95]).


lo_pattern
Pattern for lower PI column names.


hi_pattern
Pattern for upper PI column names.

title: plot_timeseries
text:
Events







Parameter
Meaning




events_global
Events that apply to all series.


events_local
Events tied to a specific unique_id.


events
Inline event column in df (boolean/string).


anomalies
Either a column name or a DataFrame of anomaly flags.


anomaly_flag_value
Value representing anomaly when using inline flag.

Parameter

title: plot_timeseries
text:
Modes



Mode
Description




overlay
All series plotted on one set of axes.


facet
Small multiples (one series per subplot).


dropdown
Single view with an interactive selector.

title: plot_timeseries
text:
Themes



Theme
Description




fa
Forecast Academy brand (default).


mckinsey
Consulting-grade clean style.


minimal
Scandinavian-style simplicity.


dark
High-contrast dark mode optimized for demos.

title: plot_timeseries
text:
Styling, Themes, & Titles

General Styling (style=)



Key
Description




title
Main chart title


subtitle
Secondary subtitle shown above the plot


x_title
X-axis label


y_title
Y-axis label


font_size
Override theme font size


font_family
Override theme font


background
Plot & paper background override





Styling Events (events_config=)
You can customize event appearance:







Key
Description




color
Vertical event line + label color


opacity
Transparency of vertical event lines


stagger_labels
Whether to stagger event labels to avoid overlap


line_width
(Optional) Width of event lines


label_font_size
(Optional) Font size of event labels





Styling Anomalies (anomalies_config=)
Customize anomaly marker appearance:







Key
Description




color
Marker color for anomalies


marker_symbol
Plotly symbol (e.g., x, circle, diamond)


marker_size
Marker size


line_width
(Optional) Border width for anomaly markers


opacity
(Optional) Opacity of anomaly markers
